items.prompt:
Which revision makes this sentence better?

Original: 'The cat sat.'

A) The cat sat and sat.
B) The small orange cat sat on the warm sunny step.
items.answer: B) The small orange cat sat on the warm sunny step.

steps: Sentence B adds details: what kind of cat (small, orange), where it sat (warm sunny step). Sentence A just repeats the same verb.

items.prompt:
Which sentence does NOT belong in a paragraph about rain?

A) Rain falls from clouds in the sky.
B) I love chocolate ice cream.
C) Plants need rain to grow.
items.answer: B) I love chocolate ice cream.

steps: The topic is rain. Sentences A and C are about rain. Sentence B is about ice cream and is off topic.

items.prompt:
Choose the better word to revise this sentence:

'The food was _____.'

A) good
B) so spicy that my eyes watered
items.answer: B) so spicy that my eyes watered

steps: 'Good' is vague. 'So spicy that my eyes watered' gives a specific, vivid detail that shows the reader what the food was like.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: 'I ran.' What question should she ask herself to add a detail?

A) Can I spell 'ran' correctly?
B) Where did I run?

steps: To add a detail, ask questions like 'where,' 'when,' 'how,' or 'why.' 'Where did I run?' leads to a better sentence like 'I ran across the playground.'

items.prompt:
Which sentence has the most detail?

A) I have a dog.
B) I have a fluffy white dog named Snowball who loves to fetch sticks.
items.answer: B) I have a fluffy white dog named Snowball who loves to fetch sticks.

steps: Sentence B answers: what kind of dog (fluffy, white), what name (Snowball), and what it does (fetch sticks). Sentence A gives no details.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: 'It was fun. I liked it. It was great.' His teacher says: 'You use the same ideas three times.' Which ONE sentence should the student keep?

A) It was fun.
B) Keep one and add a detail about WHY it was fun.
items.answer: B) Keep one and add a detail about WHY it was fun.

steps: Saying 'fun,' 'liked it,' and 'great' all mean the same thing. Cut repetition and explain WHY it was fun.

items.prompt:
Which revision adds a detail about WHERE?

Original: 'I found a shell.'

A) I found a shell and it was a shell.
B) I found a pearly white shell on the wet sand near the waves.
items.answer: B) I found a pearly white shell on the wet sand near the waves.

steps: Sentence B adds where the shell was found (wet sand near the waves) and what it looked like (pearly white).

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph. Which sentence does not belong?

'Frogs are amphibians. They start life as tadpoles. Frogs can jump very far. I had pizza for lunch.'

A) Frogs can jump very far.
B) I had pizza for lunch.
items.answer: B) I had pizza for lunch.

steps: The topic is frogs. All sentences about frogs belong. 'I had pizza for lunch' has nothing to do with frogs.

items.prompt:
Replace the word 'walked' with a better word that shows HOW the character moved:

'The tired boy walked to bed.'

A) went
B) dragged himself

steps: 'Dragged himself' shows HOW the tired boy moved — slowly and heavily. 'Went' is still vague and does not add detail.

items.prompt:
Which question helps a writer add a detail to a sentence about weather?

A) How many letters does the word 'rain' have?
B) What did the rain feel or sound like?
items.answer: B) What did the rain feel or sound like?

steps: Revision questions help writers add sensory details. 'What did the rain feel or sound like?' leads to details like 'cold' or 'drumming on the roof.'

items.prompt:
Revise this sentence by adding a detail about WHEN:

'We went swimming.'

Write the revised sentence.
items.answer: On a hot summer afternoon, we went swimming at the community pool.

steps: Add a time word like 'on a hot summer afternoon' to tell the reader when it happened.

items.prompt:
Which word is too vague in this sentence?

'The thing was pretty.'

A) The
B) thing

steps: 'Thing' does not tell the reader anything specific. Replace it with the actual name of the object (flower, sunset, painting, etc.).

items.prompt:
A partner tells you: 'I don't know what your story is about.' What is the most helpful revision to make?

A) Make the story shorter.
B) Make sure the topic is clear in the first sentence.
items.answer: B) Make sure the topic is clear in the first sentence.

steps: If a reader does not understand what the writing is about, the first sentence needs to state the topic clearly.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is an improvement over 'The bird sang'?

A) The small yellow bird sang a sweet melody from the top of the oak tree.
B) The bird sang and sang.
items.answer: A) The small yellow bird sang a sweet melody from the top of the oak tree.

steps: Sentence A adds what kind of bird (small, yellow), how it sang (sweet melody), and where (top of the oak tree). Sentence B just repeats the verb.

items.prompt:
Why do writers revise their work?

A) To change the topic completely.
B) To make the writing clearer and stronger by adding details or fixing sentences.
items.answer: B) To make the writing clearer and stronger by adding details or fixing sentences.

steps: Revision means improving what is already written. Writers add details, fix unclear sentences, and remove off-topic ideas. They do not change the whole topic.
